question: Which extra kilogram of hardware costs a two-stage rocket the most payload to orbit?
answer: One on the upper stage. It rides all the way to orbital speed, so each added kilogram costs about a kilogram of payload. A first-stage kilogram is dropped a few minutes in, far short of orbital speed, and costs only a fraction of that. That is why upper stages are thrown away.
move: Weight matters most on whatever goes the whole distance.
trap: Treating a kilogram as a kilogram wherever it rides.
reference: Humble, Henry & Larson, Space Propulsion Analysis and Design, McGraw-Hill, 1995
